notes.text: Component of the COP9 signalosome (CSN), a master regulator of the ubiquitin conjugation pathway (PubMed:26456823, PubMed:41577659). CSN mediates the deneddylation of the cullin subunits of all cullin-RING ligases (PubMed:41577659). By reversing the activating neddylation on the cullin-RING ligase, the COP9 signalosome restores the ligase to its inactive state and resets it for substrate recognition (PubMed:41577659). CSN is also involved in phosphorylation of p53/TP53, c-jun/JUN, IkappaBalpha/NFKBIA, ITPK1 and IRF8/ICSBP, possibly via its association with CK2 and PKD kinases. CSN-dependent phosphorylation of TP53 promotes degradation, while CSN-dependent phosphorylation of JUN inhibits degradation via the ubiquitin conjugation pathway. Plays a role in cell proliferation

Component of the COP9 signalosome (CSN), composed of COPS1/GPS1, COPS2, COPS3, COPS4, COPS5, COPS6, COPS7 (COPS7A or COPS7B), COPS8 and COPS9/CSNAP isoform 1; within the complex interacts with COPS1/GPS1, COPS3 and COPS8 (PubMed:41577659, PubMed:26456823). May interact with COPS5 and COPS6 (PubMed:26456823)
The Phe/Asp-rich domain at the C-terminus is necessary for its incorporation into the CSN complex, where it binds to a groove formed by COPS1, COPS3 and COPS8 (PubMed:26456823, PubMed:41577659)
Negatively regulates neddylation of proteins, including ribosoaml protein RPL11 (PubMed:23776465)

Interacts with COPS5, CUL1, CUL3 and RPL11 (PubMed:23776465). One study shows it associates with CSN (PubMed:23776465). However, another study shows it does not associate with the CSN (PubMed:26456823)
Amino acids 60-89 in isoform 2 are necessary for interaction with COPS5, CUL1, CUL3
